headline: Hired Richard Lennon as Battalion Chief, Michael Deline Jr. as Fire Captain, and William Fitzmaurice and Matthew Nolan as Fire Lieutenants.
summary: Members interviewed candidates for Battalion Chief, Fire Captain, and Fire Lieutenant in executive session. They then voted 5-0 to hire one Battalion Chief, one Fire Captain, and two Fire Lieutenants. The meeting also discussed the vacant Deputy Fire Marshal position and temporary Fire Marshal coverage, with no vote taken.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 17, 2026 meeting unanimously.
Approved hiring Richard Lennon as Battalion Chief, 5-0.
Approved hiring Michael Deline Jr. as Fire Captain, 5-0.
Approved hiring William Fitzmaurice as Fire Lieutenant, 5-0.
Approved hiring Matthew Nolan as Fire Lieutenant, 5-0.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Fire Commission Minutes         
         
Special Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, August 24, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
3rd Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda  
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER / ROLL CALL   
 The meeting was called to order by Chairman Commissioner G. Tinney at 6:05 PM. 
 
The roll was taken by the Clerk, and the following members were: 
 
Present: 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Samod Rankins 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
 
In addition, Chief Shelly Carter of the Hamden Fire Department and Briana J. Belton-
Robinson, BC Clerk, along with approximately 2 members of the public, attended virtually. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting 5, Present, Not Voting 0, Absent 0, Excused 0.  
2. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 The Commission opened the floor for public comment. No members of the public 
participating virtually or in person requested to speak. 
 
During this portion of the meeting, Commissioner R. Mordecai asked a question regarding 
the number of Fire Lieutenant positions to be filled. Commissioner S. Rankins clarified that 
the commission would interview candidates for two Fire Lieutenant positions during the 
meeting and that the remaining position would be addressed at a subsequent meeting. 
 
There being no further comments, the public comment portion of the meeting was closed. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES
A. Wednesday, June 17th, 2026 
 
  Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to approve the minutes of the June 17, 
2026 meeting. The motion was seconded by Commissioner T.A. Madera. 
 
The motion passed. 
 
Vote: All in favor, no nays, no abstentions. The previous meeting minutes were 
adopted unanimously. 
4. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.  
 
 Chairman Commissioner G. Tinney requested clarification regarding the introductory 
language appearing under the correspondence section of the agenda. The Clerk, B. 
Belton-Robinson, explained that the language was part of the standard agenda template. 
  A. Personnel Roster 
 
  Fire Chief Shelly Carter provided an update on the Fire Department and reported that 
the Department continues to move in a positive direction while responding to a high 
volume and variety of incidents, including emergency medical services, fires, motor 
vehicle accidents, rescues, and public service calls. 
 
Chief S. Carter reported that several firefighters recently completed driver 
qualifications. The Department continues to emphasize operational training and a 
return to fundamental firefighting skills. Officer development and command-and-
control training are also being prioritized to prepare newly promoted Lieutenants, 
Captains, and Battalion Chiefs. 
 
Chief S. Carter also discussed the Hamden High School Public Safety Academy, 
which introduces students to careers in fire, police, EMS, and emergency 
management. 
  B. Fire Marshal Report 
 
  Chief S. Carter discussed a recent hoarding-related matter handled by the Fire 
Marshal's Office. The Fire Marshal was working with the hospital and social service 
resources regarding the residents involved. 
 
Chief S. Carter also reported that the Deputy Fire Marshal position remains vacant. 
The two candidates previously under consideration requested that their names be 
removed from consideration. One candidate indicated that the position was not a
good fit for the candidate and their family at this time, while the other preferred to 
remain in their current position. 
 
Chief S. Carter stated that, based on discussions with Human Resources, the position 
would need to be reposted, and the selection process may need to begin again. 
 
The Commission also discussed the potential retirement of the Fire Marshal and the 
importance of maintaining appropriate Fire Marshal coverage as required by state 
statute. Chief S. Carter stated that options for temporary coverage were being 
explored, including qualified personnel within the Department and other alternatives 
permitted by applicable requirements. 
  C. Good of the Department 
 
  Chief S. Carter reported on a recent resident concern involving the handling of a 
reported gas odor. The Department subsequently responded, and Battalion Chief A. 
Barletta followed up directly with the resident to explain the appropriate information to 
communicate when reporting a gas odor or possible carbon monoxide concern. 
 
Chief S. Carter stated that the Department is working with dispatch personnel to 
improve communication and ensure that dispatchers understand the information 
necessary for fire-related calls. The Department will continue to coordinate with the 
Police Department on dispatch procedures and training. 
  D. Citizen Complaints 
 
  
 
5. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  A. Fire Commission Identification Badges 
 
  The Commission discussed identification badges for Fire Commissioners. Chief S. 
Carter requested an example of the badges previously issued to Commissioners so 
that similar badges could be produced. A photograph of a previous Commissioner's 
badge will be provided to Chief S. Carter. 
  B. Fire Commission Apparel for Community Representation 
 
  The Commission discussed obtaining polo shirts identifying members of the Fire 
Commission for use at community events. Chief S. Carter stated that the 
Department's uniform vendor was scheduled to visit the Department and that she 
would discuss producing Fire Commission polo shirts with the vendor.
Commissioners will provide their sizes once the apparel specifications are 
determined. 
6. NEW BUSINESS   
 Commissioner N. Jordan requested an update regarding accommodations and privacy for 
female firefighters within the Department's existing fire stations. 
 
Chief S. Carter stated that she had reviewed the sleeping and bathroom arrangements at 
each firehouse. Accommodations have been made at the stations where the Department's 
female firefighter is primarily assigned to provide appropriate privacy while maintaining 
integration with the crew. Chief S. Carter noted that the physical layouts of the existing 
stations limit the extent of modifications without future facility improvements. 
 
Chief S. Carter further reported that the firefighter is performing well and continues working 
toward medical control. It was explained that she must complete 30 qualifying calls before 
taking the applicable test, and that she had completed approximately 26 to 28 calls at the 
time of the most recent update. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney) 
 
 Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to enter Executive Session to conduct 
promotional interviews for the Battalion Chief, Fire Captain, and Fire Lieutenant positions. 
The motion was seconded by Commissioner N. Jordan. 
 
The motion passed. 
 
The Commission entered Executive Session to conduct the promotional interviews at 6:40 
pm. 
 
Upon completion of the interviews, the Commission returned to the public session at 9:40 
pm. 
  A. One Battalion Chief Position.  
Promotional Battalion Chief Interview Candidates: 
1. Richard Lennon 
2. Michael Dowling 
3. David Wood 
  
  
 
  B. One Fire Captain Position 
Promotional Fire Captain Interviews:
1. Nicholas Borelli 
2. Michael Deline Jr. 
3. Edward Hilbert 
  
  
 
  C. Two Fire Lieutenant Positions 
Promotional Fire Lieutenant interviews: 
1. William Fitzmaurice 
2. Christopher Parmelee 
3. Matthew Nolan 
4. Matthew Kellick 
5. Thomas Paranzino 
  
  
 
8. COMMISSION APPOINTMENT VOTES   
 
 
  A. Appointment Vote for One Battalion Chief Position 
 
  Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to hire Battalion Chief Candidate Richard 
Lennon. The motion was seconded by Commissioner R. Mordecai. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
Yes 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Samod Rankins  
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The appointment letter was enclosed with the meeting materials. 
 
Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0 
  B.  Appointment Vote for One Fire Captain Position. 
 
  Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to hire Fire Captain Candidate Michael 
Deline Jr. The motion was seconded by Commissioner N. Jordan.
Vote by Roll Call: 
Yes 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Samod Rankins  
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The appointment letter was enclosed with the meeting materials. 
 
Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0 
  C. Appointment Votes for Two Fire Lieutenant Positions 
 
  Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to hire Fire Lieutenant Candidate William 
Fitzmaurice. The motion was seconded by Commissioner T.A. Madera. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
Yes 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Samod Rankins  
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The appointment letter was enclosed with the meeting materials. 
 
Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0 
 
Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to hire Fire Lieutenant Candidate Matthew 
Nolan. The motion was seconded by Commissioner T.A. Madera. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
Yes 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Samod Rankins  
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The appointment letter was enclosed with the meeting materials. 
 
Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0
9. ADJOURNMENT   
 Commissioner S. Rankins made a motion to adjourn the meeting, and the motion was 
seconded by Commissioner R. Mordecai. 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The Fire Commission special meeting adjourned at 9:48 pm.
